title: HE RAN THE OTHER WAY.
paragraphs: Because he knew God too well.
Jonah understood something terrifying about the heart of the Lord.
And he hated the thought of it falling on them.

The brutal empire.
The nation of cruelty.
The city that crushed nations and skinned their enemies alive.
He ran west when God said east.
He fled toward Tarshish — the edge of the known world.
“But Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish from the presence of the Lord.” — Jonah 1:3
From the presence of the Lord.
Jonah knew exactly what he was doing.
This was resentment dressed as obedience avoidance.
Years later Jonah finally confessed the truth.
“I knew that You are a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.” — Jonah 4:2
Jonah ran because he knew God might forgive them.
The prophet preferred judgment over mercy.
Because mercy for your enemies feels like injustice.
And sometimes our hearts secretly whisper:
"Lord, save me… but deal harshly with them."
But you cannot outrun the voice that made the sea.
The pagan sailors began praying while the prophet slept below deck.
The unbelievers crying out to heaven.
Sometimes rebellion makes believers colder than pagans.
The Gospel Hidden in the Storm
Jonah would rather die than see his enemies saved.
But centuries later another prophet came.
He walked straight into the storm of God’s justice.
And on the cross He prayed for His enemies:
The story of Jonah is not about a fish.
Do we love mercy only when it benefits us?
Or do we rejoice when grace reaches people we think don’t deserve it?
If God only showed mercy to the deserving…
none of us would be here.
Even the ones that ran the other way.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
